newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's grains futures market pauses for breath.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's grains futures market pauses for breath.

text.p: The grains section of the Budapest Commodity Exchange paused for breath after a week-long milling wheat price surge and Wednesday's record turnover, with most of Thursday's price moves purely technical.
"Milling wheat prices have risen considerably since last week and everybody needed a break," said Imre Uzonyi of Swap brokerage. "But I think there is scope for further rises."
All milling wheat positions have surged some 3,000 forints since last Friday and on Wednesday daily grains turnover reached the year's high at 1.668 billion forints.

Turnover fell back to 501.8 million forints on Thursday and milling wheat prices were little changed except for January and March, which both rose the daily 400 forints limit to 27,750 and 27,850 forints per tonne respectively.
"There was considerable buying pressure but prices also had to rise in order to establish a normal spread between positions," Uzonyi said.
He added that rain, even if sporadic, was still delaying harvesting and fears over low quality crops prevail.
Virtually tradeless feed wheat went limit-up for all positions and Uzonyi said it was also being hit by fears of low quality and increasing worries about harvest volume.
"Earlier estimates put this year's wheat crop to some five million tonnes, but that looks less certain now," he said.
On Wednesday the agriculture ministry reaffirmed its five million tonnes estimate and said the grains lobby was driving prices up in order to extract as much state subsidy as it could.
Elsewhere, all maize prices were flat except November which rose 200 forints to 18,600 and May which lost 10 to 20,790.
Feed barley prices were mixed in minimal turnover and Uzonyi said price changes were not indicative of any trend due to the lack of interest.
He said that lacking major news, Friday would probably see sideways movements but Monday was likely to be another busy day.
"A lot can happen during the weekend and everybody will be watching weather conditions," Uzonyi said, adding "there is every chance for rainy weather over the weekend.
If that does happen, wheat prices will continue their rally on Monday".
The Met Office expected showers to move through the country from west to east with gradually clearing skies from Saturday onward.
